name: CRAFT: Customizing LLMs by Creating and Retrieving from Specialized Toolsets
venue: ICLR 2024 (paper accepted). Preprint arXiv:2309.17428 (cs.CL; cs.AI; cs.LG); v1 submitted 29 Sep 2023, v2 last revised 13 Mar 2024.
authors_affiliation: Lifan Yuan (equal contribution; work done during internship at UIUC), Yangyi Chen (equal contribution), Xingyao Wang, Yi R. Fung, Hao Peng, Heng Ji. Primary affiliation: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC).
code_url: https://github.com/lifan-yuan/CRAFT (Python; two folders: vqa built on ViperGPT, tab_and_math built on CREATOR; releases the created toolsets). Roughly 62 stars / 1 fork; last push 2024-06-03 at retrieval time.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/lifan-yuan/CRAFT (official code + released toolsets; not a continuously-updated leaderboard/paper-list; last push 2024-06-03).
task_domain: tool-use (tool creation + tool retrieval for LLMs), evaluated across three task families: vision-language (VQA), tabular processing, and mathematical reasoning. LLMs solve tasks by generating code that invokes retrieved task-specific tools (executable code snippets / APIs).
problem_setting: Plug-and-play augmentation of off-the-shelf LLMs WITHOUT any finetuning. Two phases: (1) OFFLINE tool creation - for each target task, a specialized toolset of reusable executable code-snippet tools is built by prompting GPT-4 over training examples (Generation, Abstraction, Verification, Deduplication). (2) INFERENCE-time retrieval - given a test problem, the backbone LLM (GPT-3.5-Turbo by default; also GPT-4) retrieves relevant tools from the static toolset via multi-view matching and generates/executes code conditioned on the retrieved snippets. Single-agent, non-interactive (one-shot retrieve-then-generate per problem). Supervision: training-set problems (with answers) used offline to create/verify tools; no gradient updates to the LLM or retriever. The toolset is frozen after offline construction (no test-time write-back). VQA backbone for tool execution is built on ViperGPT (uses external vision models); tabular/math built on CREATOR / Program-of-Thoughts style code execution.
what_is_retrieved: tools: reusable, abstracted, executable Python code-snippet functions (each with a function name and docstring), curated per task into a specialized toolset. The retrieved tool code is inserted into the LLM prompt so the LLM can invoke it in generated code.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a per-task specialized toolset that is induced OFFLINE (by GPT-4 over training examples) and then frozen at inference. It is an offline-induced store rather than a generic doc/KB/live-API corpus, and is NOT grown or written-back during deployment (so not episodic memory).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed small-k retrieval with a frequency/majority-vote aggregation: three candidate lists (problem-view, function-name-view, docstring-view) are merged and ranked by occurrence frequency; the top-3 most frequent tools are returned, then tools occurring only once are filtered out (so the returned set is variable-size, 0-3 tools, precision-leaning). The objective is to pinpoint the few relevant tools, not to recover a complete minimal multi-tool set nor to produce a single fixed top-k ranking; if no tool occurs more than once the retrieved set is empty and the LLM falls back to plain code generation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR). Loose mapping: Retrieve = yes (multi-view tool retrieval); Reuse = yes (retrieved tool code instantiated/invoked in the generated solution); Revise = partial/offline only (abstraction generalizes solutions during creation, but at inference the retrieved tool is used as-is, with the LLM supplying arguments rather than rewriting the tool); Retain = no (no inference-time write-back; tools are created offline). Effectively [Retrieve, Reuse].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as a tool creation + tool retrieval framework; it does not present itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: tool-API / skill-or-program: a single abstracted executable code-snippet function (function name + docstring + body) representing a reusable capability. Granularity is one tool per retrieval slot (up to three tools returned per problem).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced. Per-task toolsets are constructed offline by sampling diverse training problems (iterative similarity-based sampling with SimCSE), prompting GPT-4 to generate Python solutions, abstracting them into general tools, verifying correctness on the original problems, and deduplicating. Reported toolset sizes ~525 (VQA), ~181 (TabMWP), ~282 (MATH algebra) tools. No online/test-time induction.
index_structure_topology: Flat per-task vector index over independently-indexed tools, but with a multi-view (three-field) representation: each tool is indexed by three keys - its original creating problem (q_i), its function name (f_i), and its docstring (d_i) - and matched separately along each view. No dependency graph / hierarchy / cluster index is used for retrieval (Louvain community detection over tools is applied only as a post-hoc diversity ANALYSIS, not for retrieval).
retriever_type: Dense (embedding similarity): cosine similarity over SimCSE sentence embeddings (Gao et al. 2021) computed per view, with a majority-vote frequency aggregation across the three view-specific candidate lists. Off-the-shelf, no learned/generative retriever. (Baselines compare single-view SimCSE and BM25 retrieval over the same toolset.)
retriever_learning_signal: None / off-the-shelf. SimCSE is a pretrained sentence encoder used without task-specific training; no contrastive fine-tuning on tool-relevance labels, no LM-feedback or RL signal trains the retriever. The only learned component is SimCSE's own pretrained contrastive objective, not adapted to CRAFT.
query_construction: Synthetic, LLM-expanded multi-view query: the backbone LLM is prompted to 'describe what it needs' - given the target problem q_t, it GENERATES a hypothetical function name f_t and a docstring d_t. Retrieval then matches (q_t against creating-problems q_i), (f_t against tool function names f_i), and (d_t against tool docstrings d_i) separately, i.e. a query-expansion / HyDE-style generated-query approach across three views.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is issued per test problem before generation; no per-step or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (retrieve-then-generate): retrieval happens once per problem, after which the LLM generates and executes code. No iterative/active/adaptive re-retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per problem. There is no learned trigger, confidence signal, or agent-initiated request. (The only conditional behavior is a fallback: if the multi-view frequency filter yields an empty tool set, the LLM proceeds with plain code generation, i.e. no tools used.)
reranking: Lightweight aggregation rather than a learned reranker: the three view-specific top-k candidate lists are merged and re-ranked by frequency of occurrence (majority vote), keeping the three most frequent and discarding singletons. No cross-encoder, RRF-weighted, or instruction-tuned reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: Frequency-based filtering of the merged multi-view candidates (majority vote across three views; drop tools appearing only once). No decompose-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, or compression of the tool code; selected tool snippets are injected verbatim.
tool_document_engineering: Tools are heavily engineered OFFLINE before indexing: GPT-4 abstracts concrete solutions into general tools (replacing specific variable names with generic ones, parameterizing hard-coded textual inputs), assigns a suitable general function NAME and writes a DOCSTRING describing functionality, verifies correctness on original problems, and deduplicates. Retrieval then leverages name + docstring + creating-problem as multi-view indexing fields. No synthetic-query augmentation of the index or instruction-tuned tool embeddings (SimCSE is off-the-shelf).
index_content_separation: Partial: tools are indexed/matched via lightweight fields (function name, docstring, creating-problem text), while the heavier full code-snippet body is loaded into the prompt only for the selected tools. There is no explicit progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content protocol beyond this retrieve-then-inject-code pattern.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static toolset (frozen after offline construction); no live tool sync / CRUD / MCP / RapidAPI. Integration protocol is in-context injection of tool code, after which the LLM invokes the tools inside generated Python that is executed by an interpreter (function-calling-by-codegen). VQA tools execute via a ViperGPT-style code-execution environment with external vision models.
tool_dependency_awareness: No. Tools are treated as independent units; the retriever does not model inter-tool dependencies (output-of-A feeds B, shared prerequisites). Deduplication and diversity analysis exist, but no dependency graph or dependency-aware reranking.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + skill/tool reuse: the code snippets of up to three retrieved tools are added to the LLM prompt; the LLM then generates a code solution that invokes these tools (supplying arguments), and the combined retrieved-tool-functions + generated code are instantiated into executable code and run by an interpreter to produce the final answer. No training-signal or latent-token injection (no finetuning).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-solve with one-shot exemplar/tool injection at solve time: a single retrieval precedes a single code-generation-and-execution step. Not embedded in MCTS/tree search; no per-step interleaving or hierarchical subtask decomposition of retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: one retrieval per problem, then a single generate-and-execute pass. Retrieval is not interleaved per-CoT-step, per-sentence, or per-tool-call within a multi-step rollout.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A for CBR; mechanistically, abstraction during OFFLINE creation generalizes a specific solution into a reusable tool, and at inference the LLM adapts the retrieved tool to the new problem by composing code that calls it with appropriate arguments (verbatim tool reuse + LLM-composed invocation), not by rewriting/revising the tool itself.
retrieved_item_representation: Executable program / code snippet: each injected item is a Python tool function (name + docstring + body) inserted into the prompt as code to be invoked. Surface form is runnable code, not a free-text strategy or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural skill / reusable program at an abstracted (generalized) level: tools are deliberately abstracted from specific solutions (generic variable names, parameterized inputs, general function name + docstring) so one tool covers a class of similar problems - above raw single demonstrations but below full trajectories.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Offline quality control + multi-view voting: the Verification step discards tools that fail to solve their original problems, and Deduplication reduces redundant/confusing tools; at inference, multi-view majority voting plus the drop-singletons filter guards against weakly-matched (single-view) candidates, and an empty-set fallback avoids forcing irrelevant tools. No retriever-aware training, relevance-evaluator/self-reflection module, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: skill-library (a static, offline-built per-task toolset of reusable executable tools). It is not an episodic/working memory updated during deployment; with respect to a growing agent memory it is effectively none.
write_back: False (at inference). The toolset is created offline and frozen; the system does not store new experiences/tools during test-time deployment. (Tool creation itself is an offline batch process, not online write-back.)
online_growth: False. The retrievable toolset does not grow at test time; it is fixed after offline construction. (The paper studies scaling the toolset by adding tools from more creation epochs offline, but this is not online growth.)
write_back_trigger: never (no inference-time write-back is implemented). Offline, a tool is retained only if it passes the Verification step (i.e., it correctly solves its original creating problem) and survives Deduplication, but this is offline curation, not a runtime write trigger.
failure_experience_usage: Not used. Failed/negative experiences are not stored or retrieved. During offline creation, solutions/tools that fail verification are simply DISCARDED (success-only retention); there is no failure-only corrective memory or success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: Effectively static/append-then-dedup at creation only: the toolset is built once (with a deduplication/merge step that keeps the most comprehensive tool per group) and then frozen. No runtime delta-update, refine-overwrite, forgetting/pruning, or link-and-evolve of stored tools.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is fixed similarity-based (SimCSE cosine top-k per view) plus a frequency majority-vote aggregation; it is not a trained/RL-optimized selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private toolset per task; no cross-agent shared memory or multi-agent collaboration. The created toolsets are released and are reusable/plug-and-play across different backbone LLMs (GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4 shown), but this is reuse of a shared static resource across models, not collaborative shared memory among concurrent agents.
benchmarks: VQA: GQA, OK-VQA, A-OKVQA (visual question answering). Tabular processing: TabMWP. Mathematical reasoning: the algebra subset of MATH (881 competition-level algebra problems).
benchmark_family: Mixed: VQA / vision-language (GQA, OK-VQA, A-OKVQA); tabular reasoning (TabMWP); math reasoning (MATH-algebra). Not aligned to a single standard agent benchmark family (e.g., not Mind2Web/WebArena/ALFWorld/ToolBench); it is a tool-creation-and-retrieval evaluation across QA/tabular/math tasks.
baselines: Four baseline categories on GPT-3.5-Turbo: (1) Basic Reasoning - Chain-of-Thought (CoT, math/tabular only, no tools); (2) Tool Learning - Vanilla (ViperGPT for VQA; Program-of-Thoughts for tabular/math) and External (Vanilla + external Python libraries: NumPy, SciPy, Scikit-Image, Mahotas for VQA; Pandas, SymPy for tabular/math); (3) Different (created) Tools - LATM (Large Language Models as Tool Makers) and CREATOR; (4) Alternative Retrieval over the SAME created toolset - single-view SimCSE similarity and BM25 similarity (following ToolLLM / Gorilla style). Backbone ablation also compares ViperGPT vs CRAFT on GPT-4.
key_metrics: VQA: soft accuracy (SAcc) and F1 (open-ended generation). TabMWP: exact-match accuracy. MATH-algebra: accuracy. Analysis metrics: tool cyclomatic complexity (Lizard), number of distinct tool groups (Louvain) for diversity, and toolset-size scaling curves. No standalone Recall@k/nDCG retrieval metrics are reported.
headline_result: On GPT-3.5-Turbo, CRAFT outperforms all baseline categories, with the largest gains on VQA: SAcc 45.4 (GQA), 33.4 (OK-VQA), 30.8 (A-OKVQA) vs the ViperGPT/Vanilla baseline 35.0 / 15.4 / 15.6 - absolute SAcc improvements of +10.4 / +18.0 / +15.2 respectively. CRAFT also reaches 88.4 on TabMWP and 68.1 on MATH-algebra, generally beating Tool-Learning, tool-creation (LATM, CREATOR), and alternative-retrieval (SimCSE/BM25) baselines.
ablations: (1) Abstraction ablation: removing the abstraction step drops VQA performance markedly (e.g., GQA SAcc 45.4 -> 37.1; OK-VQA 33.4 -> 31.0; A-OKVQA 30.8 -> 28.0), confirming abstraction's importance; abstraction-ablated CRAFT still beats ViperGPT. (2) Multi-view retrieval ablation: removing any one of the three matching views (problem / function-name / docstring) degrades performance, validating multi-view matching. (3) Backbone scaling: CRAFT helps GPT-4 too (consistent gains) though less than for GPT-3.5-Turbo (hypothesis: GPT-4-created tools offer fewer insights to GPT-4 itself). (4) Toolset-size scaling: soft accuracy rises monotonically as the toolset grows (sizes 0 -> 261 -> 337 -> 525 across creation epochs). (5) Toolset analysis: low cyclomatic complexity (well-structured tools) and high diversity (e.g., 195/23/234 distinct groups out of 525/181/282 tools for VQA/TabMWP/MATH).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT reported separately; retrieval quality is assessed indirectly via end-to-end task accuracy (and by comparing alternative retrievers SimCSE/BM25 on the same toolset). Tool quality is separately analyzed via complexity/diversity, but retrieval ranking metrics are not decoupled.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (final task accuracy/SAcc/F1). Some intermediate/process analysis is reported on the artifacts themselves (tool cyclomatic complexity, tool diversity/grouping, scaling with toolset size), but not step-wise reasoning faithfulness or retrieval-precision process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Toolset construction is a one-time offline cost (estimated ~$2,500 total across all toolsets using GPT-4). CRAFT chooses GPT-3.5-Turbo (Turbo-0613) as the backbone partly for cost-effectiveness vs GPT-4. No per-query latency, token-count, or retrieval-call-count efficiency numbers are reported; the efficiency argument is that retrieval narrows a large toolset to <=3 tools to fit the prompt.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed small selection count: up to 3 tools injected per problem (the three most frequent across the three views, after dropping singletons; can be 0 if none recurs). Per-view top-k uses SimCSE similarity (k set in implementation; default views aggregated by frequency). Selection is precision-leaning / variable-size (0-3) rather than a fixed large top-k or budget-capped truncation.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (not a survey; it is a method paper with framework + experiments + analysis).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a new benchmark - CRAFT reuses existing datasets (GQA, OK-VQA, A-OKVQA, TabMWP, MATH-algebra subset of 881 problems). What it CONSTRUCTS is the toolsets: per-task tool libraries built by GPT-4 (Generation/Abstraction/Verification/Deduplication), sizes ~525 (VQA), ~181 (TabMWP), ~282 (MATH-algebra); tools verified executable/correct on their creating problems (verifiable by execution).
builds_on: Tool-creation predecessors LATM (LLMs as Tool Makers, Cai et al. 2023) and CREATOR (Qian et al. 2023); code-as-tools execution via ViperGPT (Suris et al. 2023, VQA backbone) and Program-of-Thoughts (Chen et al. 2022, tabular/math); SimCSE sentence embeddings (Gao et al. 2021) for similarity; tool-retrieval baselines from ToolLLM/ToolBench (Qin et al. 2023b) and Gorilla (Patil et al. 2023, BM25/API-name similarity). Backbone GPT-4 / GPT-3.5-Turbo (OpenAI).
contrasts_with: Approaches relying on general-purpose / human-provided fixed APIs (Toolformer, HuggingGPT, etc.) that lack task customization; prior tool-creation that produces few task-level tools without retrieval (LATM, CREATOR - small fixed tool base, no retrieval); and simplistic single-view tool-retrieval that matches only query-to-API-name similarity (ToolLLM/Gorilla, modeled here as the SimCSE and BM25 baselines). CRAFT instead builds a large customized toolset and uses multi-view (problem + function-name + docstring) retrieval.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Sits in the tool-creation + tool-retrieval lineage: extends offline LLM tool-making (LATM, CREATOR) by (a) building large, abstracted, deduplicated, verified per-task toolsets and (b) adding an inference-time multi-view dense retrieval component, moving beyond fixed general-purpose APIs and single-view API-name similarity retrieval (ToolLLM, Gorilla) toward retrieval from large specialized toolsets.
